title: Week of Sep 14 – Sep 20
subtitle: Block 3 deload. Five build weeks in a row end with a week that is lighter on purpose: 20 running miles (down from 25), lifts at 85–90% of last week's tops with fewer sets, bench active with doubles at 185 so the 225 track keeps moving, and the 5K time trial on Tuesday as the block's running benchmark. Block 4 starts Sep 21.
goals: Why deload now: your read and the log agree. Squat 215×5 (broken 3+2), RDL 235×8, bench 195×3, deadlift 300×4 'felt manageable', paused bench 165×5, pull-up max 19 on a fresh day. Every main lift moved again, which means the fatigue is banked, not visible yet. Thursday's run ('pretty exhausted, didn't feel much get up') is the first honest signal. So: tops drop 10–15% (squat 185, RDL 200, deadlift 255, OHP 105, row 125), every set at 4+ reps in reserve, nothing to failure all week. Planned sets go 87 → 73, about 16% fewer. One thing to know before you look at the volume graph: because the loads are also lighter, the app's tonnage number will read roughly 30% down (about 45k vs 65k), not 10–20%. That is what a deload is supposed to look like on that chart. Holding tonnage to only −15% would mean keeping heavy back-offs, which defeats the point. The bar goes back up Sep 21 with the loads it was already at.

Bench, road to 225: this is the 'active deload' row of the track. Wednesday is three crisp doubles at 185 after a short ramp (150×2, 170×2), 5+ in reserve, safety arms set before the first set as always. Friday is paused bench 3×3 at 150, same 2-count pause that 'was really working my chest in a different way'. No back-offs either day. Next Wednesday (Sep 23) the ramp goes to 205×2 with 2×4 at 180 behind it; if that double is 2 RIR or better the 225 attempt can move up from Oct 7 to Sep 30. OHP: 115 was the strict number this week (125 turned into a push press, your call to stop, correct). It sits at 105 this week and retests 120×5 strict in Block 4 before touching 125 again.

Running: 20 miles, your number, and it's the right one. Tue 5.5 (the 5K time trial with warm-up and cool-down) + Wed 2 + Thu 5 + Fri 2.5 + Sun 5. One quality touch this week, not two: the TT is it. Everything else is ≤150, no steady finish on Thursday, no exceptions. The easy-run HR is finally coming down: Tue 150, Wed 149, Thu 154 (down from 158 at the same distance a week earlier), Fri 147. That is the aerobic base showing up, and a deload week is where it consolidates. Tuesday is the one day HR is not the governor.

5K time trial, Tuesday: the first gate on the standing sub-90 half goal is sub-21:00 (6:45/mi). What last week says: your threshold reps ran 6:54–7:15 for 6 minutes at 170–178, and a 5K is run faster than threshold for about 20 minutes, so sub-21 is a real target and not a gift. Flat route, same one you'll use every 3 months. 1.5 easy with 3 strides, then 3.1 all-out with an even first mile (go out at 6:50, not 6:20), then a mile of jogging. Log time and average HR; the number goes in the block calendar either way. Monday's squat is 3 sets at 185, light enough that the legs will be fine.

Pull-ups and Saturday: no max set this week, that's the deload. Wed 3×6 and Sat 3×8, both around 5 in reserve, bodyweight in the weight field as usual. The max series restarts Sep 26 from 19. Push-ups are 3×15 (last week 35/20/15/10, so these are deliberately well shy), dips 3×6. Same core floor as every week (6 sets, floor only, rotated off last week): Mon = hollow hold / bird dog / bicycle crunch, Wed = side plank / V-up / shoulder taps, Fri (deadlift day) = dead bug / side plank / bird dog, Sat = flutter kicks / plank / hollow hold.

Weight and food: 189.0 Sunday, from 190.3 on Sep 6, with the 7-day trend just under 190 and the 400 deficit holding. Neither tripwire fired (easy-run HR went down, not up; every top set moved), so the deficit stays at 400 through the deload. Appetite usually dips in a lighter week; log the whole day anyway (Sunday shows 1,120 calories, which is a partial log, not a low day). Waist Sunday morning, fasted. Block 4 on Sep 21: Variation B, endurance-led, 25 → 26 → 28 miles, Saturday long run debuts at 6 miles with calisthenics condensed behind it, flat bench stays for the 225 track.
review: Build week 4 of Block 3, and the biggest week of the year. Squat 215×5 the morning after 7 miles of intervals, broken into 3+2 ('maybe could have made it with more composure'). RDL 235×8. Bench 195×3, 'had to work for it but felt better than expected', then 3×5 at 170. OHP: 115 strict, 125 became a push press and you parked it, which is the right call. Deadlift 300×4, 'felt manageable', and the honest note that lower body may have had room to push harder for a while. Paused bench 165×5, four sets, a new stimulus you could feel. Pull-up max 19 on a fresh day, then 9 and 6. Push-ups 35/20/15/10, dips 8/6/5. Lifting: 87 sets logged, about 65,500 lb, up from 83 and 62,600. Running: 20.1 miles logged through Friday plus Sunday, intervals 7 mi at 166 avg, and the easy runs finally easy: 150, 149, 154, 147. Thursday was the tell: 'pretty exhausted, didn't feel much get up.' Five build weeks. This one is the deload, and it is a real one.

days.name: 5K Time Trial · Block 3 benchmark

run.title: 5K Time Trial, 5.5 mi total
run.detail: 1.5 easy (finish with the 3 strides) → 3.1 miles all-out on a flat route you can repeat every 3 months → ~1 mile easy jog to cool down. The gate is sub-21:00 (6:45/mi). Last week's threshold reps were 6:54–7:15 for 6 minutes at 170–178 with rep 5 still at 178, and a 5K runs faster than threshold, so sub-21 is a fair target. Pacing: first mile at ~6:50, not 6:20. Mile 2 holds. Mile 3 is whatever is left. Log time and average HR in the fields; the result goes into TRAINING_CYCLE either way, this is a benchmark, not a pass/fail.
